Here’s a quick roundup of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020 (in no particular order). These picks span a range of styles—from gritty neo‑noir to high‑stakes heist thrillers—and have been celebrated by critics, audiences, and award bodies alike.

| # | Title | Director | Release Year | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Irishman** | Martin Scorsese | 2019 (U.S. theatrical release) – 2020 worldwide streaming | A masterclass in long‑form storytelling, featuring an all‑star cast (Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, Joe Pesci) and Scorsese’s signature use of de-aging tech to explore decades of organized crime. |
| 2 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | 2020 | A courtroom drama that blends political intrigue with sharp dialogue, spotlighting the 1969 anti‑war protest trial. It’s a tense, character‑driven thriller that earned multiple Oscar nominations. |
| 3 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | 2020 | A Danish film that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse, turning his life into a cat‑and‑mouse chase. It’s a psychological thriller that examines how quickly society can turn against you. |
| 4 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | 2020 | A modern retelling of the classic horror story, but with a strong crime‑thriller edge as a woman fights to prove her abuser is still after her. It’s praised for its suspenseful pacing and feminist perspective. |
| 5 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | 2019 (U.S.) – 2020 worldwide streaming | A stylish British gangster film that mixes humor with high‑stakes crime, featuring an ensemble cast and Ritchie’s trademark kinetic editing. |
| 6 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | 2020 | A historical crime‑thriller set in colonial Australia, following a woman’s quest for vengeance. It’s noted for its visceral action sequences and atmospheric tension. |
| 7 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | 2021 (U.S.) – 2020 worldwide streaming | A medieval crime‑thriller that explores themes of justice and betrayal, starring Matt Damon, Adam Driver, and Jodie Comer. It’s a tense, character‑driven narrative that earned several Oscar nominations. |
| 8 | **The Woman in the Window** | Andrew Dominik | 2021 (U.S.) – 2020 worldwide streaming | A psychological thriller about a woman who believes she witnessed a crime. It’s praised for its suspenseful pacing and strong performances. |
| 9 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | 2020 | A modern retelling of the classic horror story, but with a strong crime‑thriller edge as a woman fights to prove her abuser is still after her. It’s praised for its suspenseful pacing and feminist perspective. |
| 10 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | 2020 | A Danish film that follows a man falsely accused of child abuse, turning his life into a cat‑and‑mouse chase. It’s a psychological thriller that examines how quickly society can turn against you. |

> **Note:** Some of these films were released in late 2019 in the U.S. but became widely available in 2020 through streaming platforms or international releases.
